title: Which of sync interval, compression, delay, momentum and robust aggregation sets the final loss of low-communication training?
lede: research programme (milestone 6, results on small transformers): a predictive theory of DiLoCo-style low-communication training, testing on real small transformers the closed forms derived in about a dozen quadratic-model projects, with 16 references, hypotheses H1 to H6 and an ICML/NeurIPS workshop as the first target
summary: An open research programme rather than a finished project. DiLoCo-style training cuts communication by orders of magnitude, but choosing the sync interval, compressor and outer optimiser is still a sweep at every scale, and the best empirical scaling laws do not say why one axis costs more than another. This repository holds about a dozen closed-form results on a quadratic with gradient noise (a noise floor inflated by 1+ω under compression, a delay stability limit 2 sin(π/(4τ+2)), an optimal outer momentum that falls with the sync interval, a median that costs π/2 in variance). The programme asks whether those structural factors survive on trained transformers and compose, so that two or three measured constants per model size predict the final loss of configurations never run, as well as a refitted scaling law does. Six falsifiable hypotheses each state the result that would refute them. Milestone 1 is done: a simulated M-worker DiLoCo harness on a 0.41M-parameter GPT reproduces the synchronous loop exactly at M=1, H=1 and the quadratic closed form to 2% (ratio 0.983, 95% CI containing it). Since then, milestones 3 to 6 tested the hypotheses on a 0.41M- and a 0.92M-parameter GPT: DiLoCo at H=16 beats synchronous AdamW by 0.012 nats over 11 seeds; rand-k compression costs in proportion to ω at H=16 but is free up to ω about 8 at H=64, with H=32 in between (the cost is a function of ω and H jointly); error-feedback top-k is free to keep 1/16. Milestone 6u refuted the leading explanation for that knee: the rand-k noise per unit of ω, measured against the workers' own disagreement, is the same at every H to within 3% (E/V 1.07, 1.08, 1.11). Milestone 6v ruled out rand-k’s sparsity too: Gaussian noise with rand-k’s per-coordinate variance and nothing dropped is free at H=64 and costs at H=16, like rand-k. Results are on a character-level Shakespeare model on CPU; the research log has every pre-registered hypothesis, held or refuted.
